content:
Did something change with leantar or Cache recently?
I’m having troubles getting mathlib cache this morning: upon lake exe cache get (or lake exe cache unpack) at the decompression part, a lot of errors of the form

…/c45d87691a522094.ltar: Cross-device link (os error 18)

I thought this was because my mathlib worktrees were on a different device, so I tried to set the environment variable MATHLIB_CACHE_DIR to a location on the same device, but that did not work and the same error happens.
Nuking cache/lake does not change anything. This happens consistently on some recent PRs (e.g #38597), but funilly enough, not on master.

None of this was happening on Friday and nothing changed in my setup.

There have been two additions to the cache script on Friday, but both seem irrelevant: #37816 and #35414.

I cannot reproduce this neither on master nor when checking out #38597.

The ltar file you linked seems to be for the file Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Antidiag/Prod.lean which hasn't been updated for over a month. (That doesn't mean the ltar file is this old, dependencies of the file probably did change meanwhile!)

The cache directory should be configurable by MATHLIB_CACHE_DIR=path/to/.cache/mathlib or XDG_CACHE_HOME=path/to/.cache.

Do you have further info that could be useful for investigation? Maybe a copy of the bad ~/cache/mathlib/c45d87691a522094.ltar?

I don’t think this particular file is at fault: I gave it as an example, but whenever this happened, all decompressions failed. I already tried moving around the cache with MATHLIB_CACHE_DIR.

But now I can’t reproduce either (without even nuking or moving the cache) on the PRs that used to fail. So maybe just some transient error making me download bad files? Or a weird bug on my machine...
I’ll look for other failures during the day.

For quick reference:

  • leantar history: https://github.com/digama0/leangz/commits/master/
  • merged PRs in lean4 about leantar: https://github.com/leanprover/lean4/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aclosed+leantar+sort%3Aupdated-desc
    didn't look at these any further, maybe some of them could be meaningful
